lessons.title: Lines can be many kinds
objectives: Make marks with straight, curly, wavy and zigzag lines
Use lines to fill a leaf shape

keywords.def: a mark made by moving a pencil along the paper
a line that goes sharply up and down
a line that curves up and down like waves
how something feels, such as rough or smooth

starter: Bismillah. Draw a circle in the air with your finger.
What shapes can you see on your screen?
Name one colour you used last year.

teach.heading: Bismillah and our lines
bullets: Every drawing starts with a line
A line can be straight or curved
Take care with your pencil and paper
teach.note: Pupils need a pencil, a crayon and paper. Say bismillah. Show a straight line and a curly line on screen.

teach.heading: Types of line
teach.note: Draw each on a board and name it. Children copy in the air first, then on paper. Misconception: a line must be straight.

teach.heading: Lines in nature
bullets: A leaf has veins that look like lines
teach.note: Show a real leaf if possible. Ask what lines they see. Link to Allah's creation: attention to detail.

teach.heading: Fill the shape
bullets: Use a different line in each part
teach.note: Model drawing a leaf outline then adding three kinds of line. Encourage patience; no rubbing out needed.

practice: Draw a wavy line, then a zigzag line.
Find one straight line in your room.
independent: Draw a leaf and fill it with at least three different lines.
Fill a page with a spiral of thick and thin lines.
exit: Which line goes up and down sharply?
lessons.homework: Look at a plant or tree at home and draw the lines you see.
lessons.send: SEND: trace over dotted lines first; EAL: pair each line with its word and a gesture; stretch: add pattern inside every part of the leaf.

lessons.title: Rubbings and textures
objectives: Put textures together in a collage drawing

keywords.def: how a surface feels, such as rough or smooth
a picture made by rubbing crayon over paper on top of an object
bumpy, not smooth
flat and even to touch

starter: Name two kinds of line from last lesson.
Is a cushion rough or smooth?
Say bismillah and stroke your hand along your desk. What does it feel like?

teach.heading: Touch and describe
teach.note: Ask children to find a safe object (cloth, leaf, coin). Check no sharp or dirty items. Take turns describing.

teach.heading: Making a rubbing
bullets: Put paper on top of the object
Rub with the side of a crayon
The pattern appears on the page
teach.note: Model with a coin or leaf under thin paper. Hold the paper still with the other hand. Use the side of the crayon, not the tip.

teach.heading: Many textures, one picture
bullets: Make three rubbings on one page
Cut or fold to make a collage
teach.note: If no scissors, tear the paper carefully. Remind about safety; adult to help with scissors.

teach.heading: Show what we made
teach.note: Choose 4 children to describe their favourite texture.

practice: Is a stone rough or smooth?
Draw a wavy line and a zigzag line.
independent: Make rubbings of three different surfaces and label each.
Make a rubbing leaf picture and colour around it.
exit: Name one rough thing and one smooth thing.
How do you make a rubbing?
lessons.homework: Make a rubbing of something outside your home, with a grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: grown-up holds the paper; EAL: label textures with a picture word list; stretch: sort rubbings into rough and smooth sets.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Printing and a space buggy (Moon Zoom! and Rain & Sunrays)
lessons.title: Printing rain and sun patterns
lessons.bigQuestion: How can one small tile make a whole pattern?
objectives: To understand how a printing tile makes a repeating pattern
successCriteria: All: make a print with a tile
Most: print a pattern that repeats
Some: change the colour to make a new pattern
lessons.smsc: Cultural: repeating patterns in Islamic art

keywords.def: a picture made by pressing something with paint on it
a flat piece we print with
a small shape used again and again
do the same again
shapes in an order that repeats

hook.text: Look at a tiled floor or a wallpaper. Where does the pattern start again?

islamicLink.text: Allah sends the rain and makes the sun shine. Muslim artists showed the beauty of Allah's creation with patterns that repeat again and again, on tiles and walls. Allah is al-Musawwir, the Fashioner of every shape (al-Hashr 59:24).

starter.q: Is a tile of card hard or soft?
Name one kind of winter weather.
starter.a: For example: rain, frost, wind, snow

teach.heading: What is a print?
bullets: We press the tile on paper
The shape stays on the paper
teach.note: Show a potato or card print. Press, lift, look. Ask: what do you see? The tile's shape.

teach.heading: Rain and sun motifs
bullets: Make the motif from string on card
teach.note: Glue string in a raindrop or sun shape on a square of card. Let it dry. The string makes a raised line that prints.

teach.heading: Make it repeat
teach.note: Islamic art uses repeating patterns on tiles and walls. Show a photo of tiles. Ask: what repeats?

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share results.

check.why: Only the first one repeats the same order again.

practice.q: What comes next? sun, rain, sun, rain, ...
practice.model:
Say it aloud: sun, rain, sun, rain.
The pattern goes back to sun.
Next is sun.

practice.q: What do we do after pressing the tile?
What makes the raised line on our tile?

independent.q: Core: Make a sun or rain tile with string and card. Print it four times in a line.
independent.a: A line of four prints of the same motif
independent.model: Teacher shows it first: thin paint on the tile, press on the paper, lift straight up, move along one gap.

independent.q: Extend: Print a sun, rain, sun, rain pattern.
independent.a: Two tiles printed in an ABAB repeat

independent.q: Stretch: Print a second row in a new colour.

exit.a: A) a small shape used again and again
options: A small shape used again and again

exit.q: Big question: how can one small tile make a whole pattern?
exit.a: We print it again and again in the same order

lessons.homework: Make a printing tile from card and string and print a repeating pattern on scrap paper.
lessons.send: SEND: a ready-made tile and a sponge dabber; adult holds the paper. EAL: press, lift, repeat with actions. Stretch: make a pattern with three motifs.

Home practical guide: printing tiles with card, string and paint (portal worksheet); cover the table first
Thick card squares (from a cereal box), string, PVA glue, scissors (adult help)
Poster paint or ready-mixed paint, a plate, scrap paper

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Printing and a space buggy (Moon Zoom! and Rain & Sunrays)
lessons.title: Wheels and axles: design a space buggy
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do wheels need an axle to turn?
objectives: To understand how wheels, axles and a chassis help a vehicle move
successCriteria: All: name a wheel, an axle and a chassis
Most: say what each part does
Some: draw a labelled design of a space buggy
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: wonder at what people can invent with the minds Allah gave them

keywords.def: a round part that turns
the rod the wheels turn on
the base of a vehicle
a plan drawing of what we will make
something that carries people or things

hook.text: What would a car on the Moon need that a car at home does not?

islamicLink.text: Allah gave people animals to ride and carry loads, and says He creates things we do not yet know (an-Nahl 16:8). People later used their minds to invent wheels, cars and even a buggy for the Moon.

starter.q: Is a metal rod bendy or stiff?
Who was the first person on the Moon?

teach.heading: Look at a toy car
teach.note: Pupils turn a toy car over on camera. Ask: what holds the wheels on?

teach.heading: Three parts
bullets: Axle: the rod through the wheels
teach.note: Point to each part on a toy. Wheels and axles are a mechanism: they make movement.

teach.heading: A real Moon buggy
bullets: Astronauts drove a buggy on the Moon in 1971
teach.note: The Lunar Roving Vehicle was first used on the Apollo 15 mission in 1971. Show the photo (no people). Ask: what do you notice?

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share results.

options: The rod the wheels turn on
check.why: The base is the chassis. The axle is the rod through the wheels.

practice.q: Label the base of a vehicle.
practice.model:
The flat part at the bottom holds everything.
It is the chassis.

practice.q: How many axles does a car with four wheels usually have?

independent.q: Core: Draw your space buggy design. Label the wheels, axles and chassis.
independent.a: A drawing with three labels in the right places
independent.model: Teacher shows it first: a box for the chassis, two straws for axles, four circles for wheels, then the labels.

independent.q: Extend: Choose a material for each part from a box, straws and bottle tops.
independent.a: Chassis: box; axles: straws or skewers; wheels: bottle tops

independent.q: Stretch: Add one thing your buggy needs for the Moon.
independent.a: For example: a box to carry Moon rocks or an aerial

exit.q: Big question: why do wheels need an axle to turn?
exit.a: The axle holds the wheels on and lets them spin

lessons.homework: Collect a small box, two straws and four bottle tops for next lesson's buggy.
lessons.send: SEND: a real toy car to hold and label stickers. EAL: wheel, axle, chassis with pictures. Stretch: explain why the wheels must be the same size.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Printing and a space buggy (Moon Zoom! and Rain & Sunrays)
lessons.title: Make and test a space buggy
lessons.bigQuestion: How can we make our buggy roll further?
objectives: To understand how to make, test and improve a simple vehicle
successCriteria: All: make a buggy that rolls
Most: test how far it rolls
Some: say one way to make it better
lessons.smsc: Moral: honest testing and trying again

keywords.def: build what we designed
try it to see if it works
say what went well and what to change
the rod the wheels turn on
the base of a vehicle

hook.text: Your buggy will not roll. What could be wrong?

islamicLink.text: Allah loves that when one of us does a job, we do it well and carefully. We make our buggy with care, test it honestly and try again. Trying our best is part of good character (ihsan).

starter.q: The base of a buggy is the:

starter.a: Holds the wheels and lets them turn

starter.q: What did you collect for today?
starter.a: A box, two straws and four bottle tops

teach.heading: Make the axles
bullets: Push two straws through the box
teach.note: Show how an adult makes holes with a pencil in a small box. The straws must be level and parallel.

teach.heading: Add the wheels
bullets: An adult makes a hole in each bottle top
Push a skewer or straw through
teach.note: Safety: adults use sharp things. Wheels must not rub on the box.

teach.heading: Test it
bullets: Let it roll down a book ramp
teach.note: Same ramp and same push each time to keep it fair.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share results.

check.q: The wheels rub on the box. What should we do?
options: Move the wheels a little away from the box
check.why: Wheels need a gap so they can turn freely.

practice.q: Our buggy rolled 3 hand spans, then 5, then 4. Which roll was best?
practice.model:
Look at the numbers: 3, 5, 4.
The biggest is 5.
So the second roll went furthest.

practice.q: Why do we use the same ramp each time?

independent.q: Core: Make your buggy and test it on a book ramp three times.
independent.a: A working buggy and three hand-span results
independent.model: Teacher shows it first: book ramp, put the buggy at the top, let go (no push), count hand spans.

independent.q: Extend: Say one thing that went well.
independent.a: For example: the wheels turned freely

independent.q: Stretch: Say one thing you would change.
independent.a: For example: straighter axles, bigger wheels, a lighter box

exit.a: A) say what went well and what to change
options: Say what went well and what to change

exit.q: Big question: how can we make our buggy roll further?
exit.a: For example: make the axles straight and let the wheels turn freely

lessons.homework: Test your buggy on a different floor (carpet, then a smooth floor) and tell an adult where it rolled further.
lessons.send: SEND: pre-made holes and wheels; pupil assembles and tests. EAL: make, test, change with actions. Stretch: test a bigger and smaller wheel and compare.

A small box, two straws, two wooden skewers (adult only), four bottle tops, sticky tape
A book to make a ramp
Buggy test record: three hand-span results (portal printable)
